description: SRL-2018 compromised enterprise network. Admin server memory dump (5 GB, 2018-09-07). Volatility3 analysis reveals: 2 PowerShell processes (PIDs 1160, 11008) both spawned from PID 6252 — classic C2 process tree. Evidence SHA-256: d58343cb4e4a06ecc56012c8e25760b297594bf4695303527a5cbb2331726891. Malfind: 31 processes with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE regions — widespread code injection. Consistent with post-exploitation framework (Cobalt Strike / Meterpreter) active in memory.

acquisition.source_dataset: SANS Find Evil! 2026 — SRL-2018 Compromised Enterprise Network

artifacts.description: 2 PowerShell processes (PIDs 1160, 11008) both children of PID 6252. PID 1160 started 2018-07-29T12:59:22Z, PID 11008 started 2018-08-13T17:23:27Z. Same parent spawning multiple PowerShell instances over weeks is consistent with persistent C2 beacon or lateral movement tooling.

31 processes with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE memory regions not backed by files on disk. Scale of injection (31 processes) is consistent with a framework-level injector such as Cobalt Strike, Meterpreter, or similar post-exploitation tool performing reflective DLL injection across the process tree.
Windows x64 system. Kernel base 0xf8032461e000, DTB 0x1aa000.
Network connections active at time of acquisition. Admin server with active connections to internal domain infrastructure consistent with post-exploitation lateral movement.

forensic_anomalies: 2 PowerShell processes from same parent (PID 6252) — persistent C2 process tree
31 processes with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE — framework-level reflective injection
PowerShell span dates: July-August 2018, dump September 2018 — weeks of persistence
devil_advocate: PowerShell is commonly used for legitimate admin tasks — parent PID could be a scheduled task runner
PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE is a common malfind false positive for JIT-compiled code (.NET, Java)
